# Video-editor test-media corpus

Generated by [`tools/gen-test-fixtures.py`](../../../../tools/gen-test-fixtures.py)
(ffmpeg-dependent, run locally — see
[`docs/specs/video-editor/11-testing-phasing.md` §2](../../../../docs/specs/video-editor/11-testing-phasing.md)).
CI consumes these committed files; it does not regenerate them (no `ffmpeg`
at generation-time is required in CI, only at decode-time for the tests that
need a real container/codec — see §3.4 of the same doc).

Regenerate the whole corpus with:

```
python3 tools/gen-test-fixtures.py
```

Total corpus size: **~2.5 MiB** (`du -sh crates/photonic-video/tests/fixtures`),
comfortably inside the 5 MB corpus budget and the combined 10 MB
`tests/golden/` + fixtures budget (§1.5).

## Fixtures

### `color_bars.mp4`

Deterministic known-value video source for probe-metadata tests (CAP-001).

- 4s, 320×180, `yuv420p`, H.264, 30fps (`smptebars` source, static — compresses
  to ~5 KiB)
- Probed: `codec_name=h264 width=320 height=180 pix_fmt=yuv420p r_frame_rate=30/1 duration=4.000000`

### `counter.mp4` + `frame_truth.json`

Frame-number burn-in (`drawtext`, `%{n}`) for seek-accuracy tests. One
keyframe every 2s (GOP=60) so seeks exercise the GOP-seek path.

- 10s, 320×180, 30fps, 300 frames, keyframes at frame indices `0, 60, 120,
  180, 240` (verified via `ffprobe -show_entries frame=key_frame`)
- Probed: `codec_name=h264 width=320 height=180 pix_fmt=yuv420p r_frame_rate=30/1 nb_frames=300 duration=10.000000`
- `frame_truth.json` records the burn-in convention: frame *N* (0-based)
  has `str(N)` burned in top-left. No separate ground-truth values are
  needed beyond the frame index itself.

### `beep_flash.mp4` + `beep_flash.wav`

A/V sync ground truth (CAP-004/SS-1 test hook). Video flashes white for
exactly 1 frame every 1s (frame *N* is white iff `N % 30 == 0`); audio has
a 5ms 1kHz beep at the same wall-clock instants.

- Video: 60s, 320×180, 30fps, 1800 frames, `yuv420p`/H.264
  Probed: `codec_name=h264 width=320 height=180 pix_fmt=yuv420p r_frame_rate=30/1 nb_frames=1800 duration=60.000000`
- Audio: 60s, 48kHz, mono, **IMA ADPCM** (not raw PCM — see note below)
  Probed: `codec_name=adpcm_ima_wav sample_rate=48000 channels=1 duration=60.000000`
- Verified beep onset survives ADPCM: `astats` RMS level in a 15ms window
  centered on t=1.0s is **-7.93 dB**, vs **-inf dB** (silence) in an
  off-instant window — the transient is cleanly detectable for an
  RMS-threshold onset detector.

**Size note:** 11 §2's table lists an approximate `< 1 MB` budget for this
row. That figure isn't reachable for 60s of raw 16-bit PCM at 48kHz mono
(~5.7 MB, by itself over the whole corpus's 5 MB budget) — WAV's only
in-format compression is a lossy codec like ADPCM. `beep_flash.wav` uses
`adpcm_ima_wav` (~1.4 MB, ~4:1 vs raw PCM) as the practical floor that
still (a) writes a real `.wav` with the exact required `sample_rate=48000
channels=1`, and (b) preserves beep-onset timing (verified above). Combined
with the 47.6 KiB video, this pair is ~1.46 MB, not <1 MB — the corpus-wide
5 MB budget (§2's own stated total) is what actually governs, and the full
7-file corpus stays at ~2.5 MB, well inside it.

### `vfr_sample.mp4`

Variable-frame-rate source — exercises `FrameRate::is_exact()`'s warning
path and non-integral `ticks_per_frame` rounding.

- 8s total: first 4s at 24fps (96 frames), then 4s at 30fps (120 frames),
  216 frames total. Built by joining two constant-rate lavfi segments with
  the `concat` **filter** (not the concat demuxer's `-c copy` stream-copy
  mode, which was tried first and silently mis-timestamps the second
  segment's frames onto the first segment's time_base — verified by
  dumping per-frame `pts_time` and finding a spurious 1s gap plus uniform
  24fps spacing straight through the 30fps segment; the filter path gives
  clean per-segment PTS spacing instead).
- Probed: `codec_name=h264 width=320 height=180 pix_fmt=yuv420p r_frame_rate=24/1 nb_frames=216 duration=8.000000`
  (`r_frame_rate` reports the container's overall rational approximation;
  the container is genuinely variable — per-frame `pts_time` deltas are
  `1/24` for the first 96 frames and `1/30` for the remaining 120, not a
  single constant.)

### `alpha_gradient.mov`

Straight-alpha ramp with known values (CAP-021 transparent-export
correctness). Constant blue fill (`r=0 g=0 b=255`), alpha ramping
`0 -> 255` left to right (`a = (x/width)*255`).

- 3s, 160×90, 30fps, 90 frames, `qtrle` codec, `argb` pixel format
  (lossless, alpha-capable; far smaller than ProRes 4444 at this
  resolution, so used instead of the spec's `yuva444p`/ProRes 4444
  alternative)
- Probed: `codec_name=qtrle width=160 height=90 pix_fmt=argb r_frame_rate=30/1 nb_frames=90 duration=3.000000`
- Verified ramp on frame 0 (`rgba` raw extraction): `x=0` → alpha `0x00`,
  `x=80` (mid) → alpha `0x7f` (127), `x=159` (right edge) → alpha `0xfd`
  (253); RGB constant `(0, 0, 255)` at all three sample points.

### `multi_audio.mkv`

3 discrete audio streams (dialogue/music/fx) with different channel counts.

- 15s, Opus-encoded (small, lossy but fine for synthetic sine-tone
  fixtures), audio-only Matroska container
- Stream 0 (dialogue): mono, 440Hz sine — `codec_name=opus sample_rate=48000 channels=1 channel_layout=mono`
- Stream 1 (music): stereo, 220Hz left / 330Hz right — `codec_name=opus sample_rate=48000 channels=2 channel_layout=stereo`
- Stream 2 (fx): true 5.1 (6ch), 110Hz sine duplicated across all 6
  channels — `codec_name=opus sample_rate=48000 channels=6 channel_layout=5.1`
- Container duration probes at `15.008s` (Opus encoder pre-skip/padding,
  not a bug — the synthesized source signal is exactly 15s).

### `channel_swap_rgb_to_gbr.cube`

Known-transform 3D LUT for `apply_lut` / CAP-015 coverage (29 §6 gap 2). A
`LUT_3D_SIZE 2` (8-entry, ~130 B) pure channel swap **RGB → GBR**: input
`(r, g, b)` maps to output `(g, b, r)`.

- Domain `0..1` on all channels; entries in `.cube` red-fastest order
  (`data[r + g*2 + b*4]`, the order documented at
  `crates/photonic-render/src/lut.rs:18-20`).
- Because a coordinate permutation is *linear*, size-2 trilinear interpolation
  reproduces it **exactly**, so downstream assertions are byte-level, not
  tolerance-based (e.g. sampling `(0.25, 0.5, 0.75)` returns `(0.5, 0.75, 0.25)`).
- Parsed + sample-checked by `parse_channel_swap_fixture_exact_sample` in
  `crates/photonic-render/src/lut.rs`; consumed by AS-2's `apply_lut` step.

Not ffmpeg-generated — a hand-authored text file, regenerated by editing it
directly (it is tiny and fully specified above).

### `title_asset.photon` + `title_doc_asset.photon`

Vector `.photon` timeline fixtures for the acceptance stories (29 §3 fixture
table). Authored via the `photonic_core::Document` builder, generated by the
checked-in dev tool:

```
cargo run -p photonic-render --example gen_p1_golden_fixtures -- video-fixtures
```

(The `video-fixtures` arg writes ONLY these two files and does **not** touch the
31-case golden corpus.)

Node ids are **hardcoded** (deterministic) so the AS scripts can address nodes
by id; the top-level `layers`/`nodes` map key *order* may still vary between
runs because `save_photon` serialises `Document`'s HashMaps directly — that
affects only byte order, not loading, node resolution, or rendering.

- **`title_asset.photon`** (AS-1 title clip) — one text node:
  - `title` — id `11a50000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`, solid white fill.
    AS-1 fades the *clip* in via the timeline `transform.opacity` PropPath.
- **`title_doc_asset.photon`** (AS-3 keyframed title) — two stably-named nodes,
  each with a solid fill so `node.<id>.fill.color` has a real target:
  - `title_line` — id `11d00000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001` (AS-3 keyframes
    this node's `fill.color`).
  - `subtitle_line` — id `11d00000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002`.

Loaded + validated by `vector_title_fixtures_load_and_expose_keyframe_targets`
in `crates/photonic-video/tests/preview_media_load.rs`. Both are well under
11 §2's ≤5 MB corpus budget (~3–5 KB each).

## Regenerating a single fixture

The script has no per-fixture CLI flag; it always regenerates the whole
corpus. To iterate on one fixture during development, comment out the other
entries in the `generators` list in `tools/gen-test-fixtures.py` temporarily,
or copy the relevant `ffmpeg` invocation out of the corresponding `gen_*`
function and run it directly from this directory.
